songs.name: I've Been All Around This World

ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic gems lead into soaring Dark Star and electric fire
ai_show_review.blurb: The first set showcases intimate acoustic numbers like Little Sadie and The Master's Bouquet before shifting to an electrified second half. Highlights include a transcendent Dark Star that segues into New Speedway Boogie and a rousing Turn On Your Lovelight, with standout organ textures from Tom Constanten. Jerry’s 1969 Strat tone and Phil’s Alembic‑modified EB‑0 bass drive the jams.
ai_show_review.review:
December 26, 1969 at McFarlin Auditorium finds the Dead in peak transition mode – a quiet acoustic set that blossoms into an electric blaze. The band opens with folk‑leaning cuts such as Little Sadie, Long Black Limousine and the haunting "I've Been All Around This World," then pivots seamlessly with Uncle John's Band into a second set that crackles with energy. 
The centerpiece is a soaring Dark Star, where Jerry’s brown‑sunburst Strat sings over Tom Constanten’s trippy organ swirls, while Phil’s Alembic‑modified bass underpins the improvisation. The jam rolls straight into a fiery New Speedway Boogie and culminates in an exuberant Turn On Your Lovelight, each moment captured with crystalline clarity on the Warner‑Evans soundboard. Jerry’s guitar tone is silky yet full of ideas, Bob’s harmonies lock tight on the acoustic numbers, and the dual drummers keep a propulsive groove that never loses its swing. For anyone looking to hear this historic acoustic‑electric pivot at its best, the "gd1969-12-26.sbd.warner-evans.28448.sbeok.flac16" recording offers unrivaled fidelity and balance.

best_recording.reason: Exceptional crystal‑clear soundboard capture that highlights the acoustic gems and soaring Dark Star with minimal flaws

song_highlights: I've Been All Around This World

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s classic ’69 Strat tone is silky and full of inventive leads, especially on the Dark Star climax.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh delivers a powerful, Alembic‑modified EB‑0 bass line that anchors both acoustic and electric sections, locking in solidly after a brief late start.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocal harmonies are spot‑on throughout, adding depth to Uncle John's Band and the acoustic numbers.
band_performance.Tom: Constanten’s organ work is inspired and trippy, providing rich texture on China Cat Sunflower, Dark Star, New Speedway Boogie, and Lovelight.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s percussion adds subtle color and drive, complementing the rhythmic flow of the set.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann supplies a steady, propulsive groove that keeps the band tight during high‑energy jams.
